claims.exact_claim: Section 5.21 of Milne's SVp.pdf (v2.2, cited in OpenAI Family 001) proves the required lifting theorem with additional Hodge structure needed for lem:admissible-realization.
hypotheses: The actual supplied Section 5.21 concerns A/Qbar with good reduction at w and a Hodge class gamma extending as a global section in a family with additional structure.
The needed lift must be a CM lift of the special fiber inside that same additional-structure family.
The graph names v2.2, but the inspected text is v2.4.
claims.reason: The inspected passage says to complete the proof by showing the required CM lift in the family and calls that task more general than known or even conjectured results.
claims.version_limitation: No v2.2 text was supplied or inspected; no assertion that its exact wording or section numbering was independently checked is made.

claims.exact_claim: Kisin (2017) Proposition 1.4.15 alone suffices to establish lem:admissible-realization without proving that a single fixed-marking algebraic quasi-isogeny simultaneously realizes the prescribed crystalline filtration and preserves all prime-to-p structure tensors.
hypotheses: Original Hodge-type setting with an embedding into a Siegel datum.
Hyperspecial p-level from a reductive model and sufficiently small prime-to-p level.
Original source has p>2 in Section 1.1 and main Theorem 0.3; Proposition 1.4.15 invokes that framework and does not provide a p=2 extension.
x and x' are special-fiber points in the source's isogeny-class setting, equipped with weak polarizations and the canonical tensor families.
claims.actual_theorem: Same isogeny class if and only if there exists one weak-polarization-respecting quasi-isogeny carrying both the crystalline and every prime-to-p tensor family to their counterparts.
claims.reason: Existence of some simultaneously tensor-preserving map does not identify a previously fixed crystalline marking or preserve a separately prescribed pullback filtration.
claims.mathematical_check: If b1=b0*u for a different quasi-isogeny, then b1^* Fil_y=u^*(b0^* Fil_y). Nothing in Proposition 1.4.15 states that u stabilizes the prescribed filtration.

supported_scope: Rejection of the two Argus source-based shortcuts as proofs of prescribed fixed-marking realization.
Milne v2.4 Section 5.21 is a proposed route with an explicitly unfinished lifting step.
Milne v2.4 Section 12 uses September 23 manuscript numbering and is not an independent verification of the October 7 realization lemma.
Kisin Proposition 1.4.15 genuinely characterizes existence of one simultaneously tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny in its original setting.
The old realization_proof.md source-discussion corrections are supported within these source and version boundaries.
limitations: The historical v2.2 Milne text was not inspected; v2.4 cannot be retroactively assigned to it.
No proof or disproof of the surrounding manuscript realization lemma is delivered.
No KZ/PR/GLX geometric steps or alternate p=2 extension are investigated.
Milne's actual theorem 6.19 is not reviewed; its mention under some hypotheses does not certify the graph shortcut.
No novelty verification or new manuscript-error search was performed.
The preceding chatbot conversation in SVp-section12.txt lines 1-46 is not treated as Section 12 commentary or an external theorem.
concrete_obligations: Attribute every Milne passage to the inspected v2.4; verify the exact historical v2.2 before making claims specifically about its text.
Supply the additional-Hodge-structure-preserving lifting theorem rather than citing a proposed proof step.
For a Kisin-based route, identify the actual crystalline marking of the same algebraic quasi-isogeny that preserves the prime-to-p tensors and prove the prescribed filtration equality.
Check the original prime and level restrictions; provide separate applicable mathematics for p=2.
Keep rational admissibility separate from integral lattice/tensor realization; the arbitrary stable-lattice route belongs to the lattice-obstruction unit.
